div.l: And wel I wot / as ye gon · bi the weye
Ye shapen yow / to Iapen and to pleye
For treuly comfort ne merthe / is it noon ·
To ryden by the weye / doomb as the stoon ·
And therfor wol I make / yow disport
As I seyde erst and doo yow som comfort
And if yow liketh all / bi on assent
For to stondyn / at my Iugement
And for to werkyn · / as I shal . yow seye
To morwyn̄ whan · / ye rydyn bi the weye
Now bi my fadrys soule / that is dede
But ye be mery / I yeve yew myn heed
Holdeth vp your handys / with outēn more speche
Owr coıı̄unsel was / nat longe for to seche
Vs thouhte it was nat worth / to make it wis
And graıı̄untyd hym · / withoute more avis
And bad hym · seye / hys wordys as hym leste
Lordynges qdquod he / now now herkeneth for the beste
But taketh itit nat / I pray yow in disdayne
This is the poynt / to speke shoort and pleyne
That eche of yow / to short with youre weye
In this viage / shal tellen talys tweye
To Cantirbury ward / I mene It soo
And homward / he shal tellyn othir too
Of aventures / that somtyme have bi falle
And which of yow / bereth hym best of alle
That is to seye / that telleth in this caas
Talis of sentence / and most solas
Shal have a souper / at our althyr cost
Heer in this place / syttyng bi this post
Whan that ye comyn · / a gayne fro Cantirbury
And for to make yow / the more mery
I wol my self goodly / with yow ryde
Vp on myn owne cost / and be yowr guyde
